From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 16:48:00 +0000
Subject: Preliminary findings — RetailEdge latency spike

Quick notes from the bridge and initial logs:
- Timeline: spike begins 15:44 UTC coincident with RetailEdge promo traffic surge.
- Root cause (short): cache key cardinality explosion after promo caused KV-store thrashing + elevated memory pressure on the inference pool. Several worker processes experienced transient OOM and returned 502/503.
- Impact: increased p95/p99 latency for generation routes (checkout recommendations) and ~3.8% error rate for requests during 15:44–16:20 UTC.

Short-term actions taken (done by 16:30 UTC):
- Rolled back to prior model shard configuration (pinned variant).
- Increased per-worker memory limit and disabled a recent aggressive batching optimization for the affected route.
- Warmed KV cache for top-100 prefixes observed in the promo traffic.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Collect and upload raw traces (neha_kapoor) — query_logs.zip attached.
- Run a targeted load test against canary config (ben_carter) — expected complete by 18:00 UTC.
- Draft RCA for exec/customer (jonas_weber) — will produce a PDF by EOD.

Attachment: query_logs.zip (contains traces and span samples)

—Ben

Date: Wed, 3 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: RCA & remediation sprint plan — RetailEdge incident (attached)

Team / RetailEdge,

Attached is the formal RCA and remediation sprint plan. Executive summary:
- Primary cause: KV cache key cardinality spike due to unanticipated product feed prefix churn during the promotional window. The resulting increased memory pressure triggered transient OOMs in worker processes and caused elevated error rates and tail latency.
- Contributing factors: recent batching heuristic (v2) reduced per-request memory headroom; monitoring alert thresholds didn’t catch cache-key cardinality growth pattern early enough.

Remediation sprint (owners / due dates):
1) Workload hardening — implement prefix normalization and controlled shard allocation (owner: ben_carter) — due 2028-07-08
2) Memory safety guardrails — add per-request memory budget checks and fast-fail fallback (owner: neha_kapoor) — due 2028-07-06
3) Monitoring / Alerting — new cardinality metric and high-cardinality alert (owner: jonas_weber) — due 2028-07-05
4) Operational playbook — rollback and canary checklist improvements, and a pre-promotional traffic runbook with RetailEdge (owner: karthik_iyer) — due 2028-07-09

Attachments: retailedge_rca.pdf, remediation_sprint.md
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RE-5912

I’ll follow up with a short executive readout doc by EOD and owners will post progress to the RE-5912 ticket.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Reliability Engineering
